Name: Jessica Kennedy
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

I feel my students would benefit from being able to break down parts of science articles to better understand what is being discussed. Some science texts are harder to understand so by being able to select pieces of the text and form questions or responses, students can pull out what they understand and what they are having trouble understanding.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

I will use partner talk along with the annotation method with articles and visuals in my science classroom. Scientific texts can be difficult to read and understand so I will have the students use the annotation method then partner talk to deepen their understanding.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:

I need help finding quality scientific articles to use in the classroom other than reading from the textbook.
